title: Oracle Database Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Oracle Database course.

entries.name: Ask DUAL for a calculation
entries.summary: DUAL is a small built-in table used when a query needs no real table data.

entries.name: Choose number and text types
entries.summary: Oracle types describe the values a column or expression holds.

example.code: SELECT CAST(12 AS NUMBER(3)) AS pages, CAST('Moon Trip' AS VARCHAR2(40)) AS title FROM dual;

entries.name: Build a small query-only list
entries.summary: A WITH query gives a temporary name to a result used by that statement.

example.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',60 FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'Tiny Seed',20 FROM dual)
SELECT title,pages FROM books ORDER BY pages;

entries.name: Fetch the first sorted row
entries.summary: FETCH FIRST limits rows after the chosen order.

example.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',60 FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'Tiny Seed',20 FROM dual)
SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY pages,title FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY;

entries.name: Write an unambiguous date
entries.summary: A DATE literal names a calendar date in a fixed form.

example.code: SELECT TO_CHAR(DATE '2026-11-16','YYYY-MM-DD') AS club_day FROM dual;

entries.name: Handle a missing value
entries.summary: NULL means a value is missing or unknown.

example.code: SELECT NVL(CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR2(20)),'Not chosen') AS book_choice FROM dual;

entries.name: Join a book and its author
entries.summary: A join combines records whose key values match.

example.code:
WITH authors(id,name) AS (SELECT 1,'Mia' FROM dual), books(title,author_id) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',1 FROM dual)
SELECT b.title,a.name FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id=b.author_id;

entries.name: Count a category
entries.summary: GROUP BY makes one result per category. COUNT counts rows belonging to that category.

example.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (SELECT 'story' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'story' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'science' FROM dual)
SELECT kind,COUNT(*) AS total FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;

entries.name: Create an identity key
entries.summary: An identity column lets Oracle create a numeric id.

entries.name: Read a sequence value
entries.summary: A sequence is a separate object that gives out numbers.

example.code:
CREATE SEQUENCE cma_book_numbers START WITH 100 INCREMENT BY 1;
SELECT cma_book_numbers.NEXTVAL AS number_value FROM dual;

entries.name: Run a small PL/SQL block
entries.summary: PL/SQL adds variables and step-by-step instructions to Oracle SQL.

entries.name: Undo uncommitted sample changes
entries.summary: A savepoint marks a point inside a transaction.
